title: Per-tenant lane trace muxer with schema-evolution compatibility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a tenant-aware trace muxer that routes incoming spans into per-tenant processing lanes and performs live schema evolution so downstream exporters (Tempo/Jaeger/third-party) receive compatible envelopes. This component should isolate tenant routing, normalize span schemas (v0/v1 protobufs and legacy tags), and provide a pluggable adapter interface for backend-specific formatting. Goal: enable zero-downtime migration to new span schema while preserving routing guarantees and improving per-tenant observability controls.
acceptance_criteria: Muxer can concurrently route spans for at least 500 tenants with predictable latency (<10ms median routing overhead) under load
Schema adapter layer supports both legacy(span_v0) and new(span_v1) protobuf shapes and can be extended without restarts
Unit+integration tests cover tag renaming, traceid padding, and sampling marker preservation across adapters
Two backend adapters implemented: a Tempo-compatible envelope and a compact Jaeger-compatible payload
Canary rollout plan documented and validated in staging with canary tenants showing no more than 1% end-to-end span loss
Operational metrics emitted: per-tenant routed_spans, schema_conversion_errors, adapter_latency_ms (p50/p95), backpressure_events
notes_and_progress: 2026-03-01: Kickoff — scope agreed: router core + schema adapter API + 2 adapters (tempo/jaeger).
2026-03-03: Decided on a lightweight in-memory tenancy map with bloom-filtered fast-path for high-volume tenants to avoid lock contention.
2026-03-04: PoC runtime shows p50 routing overhead ~6ms with 200 concurrent tenants. PoC repo: github.com/redwood-inference/obs-tenant-muxer/pull/8.
2026-03-06: Design review feedback from infra (Marta Ortiz): prefer explicit schema version header vs magic field detection. Updated proto bridges accordingly.
2026-03-07: Security review kickoff — SRE requested an audit of how tenant IDs are preserved when sampling markers are rewritten. Assigned to security_contact@example.com.
2026-03-08: Implemented initial adapter interface (AdapterV2) and tempo adapter scaffold. Integration test harness created to replay real traffic traces stored in test-data/traces/.
2026-03-09: Discovered conversion edge-case: legacy tags with nested JSON previously stored in attribute string. Added normalization step to flatten or preserve payloads behind a feature flag.

2026-03-10: Began writing migration playbook: zero-downtime strategy uses per-tenant opt-in to new schema followed by gradual global flip. Draft at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Tenant+Muxer+Migration+Playbook.
Next steps: complete Jaeger adapter, add end-to-end canary in staging, add RBAC checks for tenant-lane configuration, finalize security sign-off.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Schema conversion could be CPU-heavy for high-cardinality tag sets. Mitigation: add fast-path that copies spans when no conversion needed and offload complex conversions to a bounded worker pool.
Risk: Tenant misrouting during rollout. Mitigation: ship audit logs and per-tenant replay tool to reprocess misrouted spans.
Risk: Backpressure to upstream collectors. Mitigation: implement circuit-breaker per-adapter and durable buffering with configurable retention limits.
Risk: Compatibility gaps with third-party backends. Mitigation: adapter test matrix and contract tests against real Tempo/Jaeger docker images in CI.
qa_plan: Synthetic replay of 24h production trace window against staging muxer and both adapters
Canary with 5 tenants for 48h: verify trace completeness and downstream dashboards
Chaos tests: temporary adapter failures to validate retry/backoff and no data duplication
Load test: 100k spans/s sustained for 10 minutes to validate latency and backpressure metrics
